newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan rubber market seen drifting in ranges.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan rubber market seen drifting in ranges.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures markets are likely to drift within limited ranges in directionless trade this week, traders said on Monday.
They said the markets would get few clues from moves in currencies and overseas markets.

"Activity this week will be dull. Sellers will be cautious of selling aggressively from the current levels, while the continued oversupply trends in Japan would prompt market players to sell on any price rally," one trader said.

Traders said the benchmark March contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) was expected to move within a range of 130 and 136 yen per kg this week, sandwiched between short-covering and selling on any price recovery.
The benchmark March contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 133.5 yen per kg, down from Friday's close of 134.3 yen.
Similarly on the Kobe Rubber Exchange, the key March contract was 133.4 yen per kg, down from Friday's close of 134.2 yen.
Some traders said, however, that the rubber markets could head south if they break out of the ranges as bumper rubber stocks hit market sentiment.
Traders said rubber stocks have yet to reach their ceiling, although growth has slowed down slightly.

"I would not rule out a possibility that TOCOM's benchmark March will break under the 130 yen level. Until stocks show signs of declining, a full-fledged recovery in Japan's rubber markets is unlikely," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
The analyst said current stock levels were about 60 percent higher than what was appropriate, and that stocks would rise to 52,000 or 53,000 tonnes by November.

Japanese rubber stocks at designated warehouses rose to 47,873 tonnes at the end of September, rising 209 tonnes from mid-September but falling short of the market's previous expectation of 50,000 tonnes.
Japanese rubber futures markets posted a moderate technical rebound last week due to the lower-than-expected rise in stocks.
Thai rubber offer prices to Japan were quoted at around 122 U.S. cents on a free-on-board (FOB) basis as of Monday, unchanged from October 7.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber to large-lot end users was quoted at 144 yen per kg as of Monday, also unchanged from October 7.
